# stream-upstream-failover-runtime

Repository-authored, sanitized NGINX migration fixture for issue #367 ([MIG-06] gRPC/FastCGI/uWSGI/L4 migration E2E lanes), amendment requirement "backend unavailable/recovery behavior through the normal resilience path" for the bounded stream translation (#426). It uses only synthetic loopback addresses; it contains no production configuration, credentials, or external endpoints.

The exact assessment contract, candidate disposition, categories, origin, and license are recorded in `manifest.json`. It reuses #426's `stream { upstream {} }` → HTTP upstream translation (a stream server's named upstream is emitted into the same `[[upstreams]]` array an HTTP `proxy_pass` upstream would use) together with #365's per-backend `max_fails`/`fail_timeout` → shared `[upstreams.resilience]` circuit-breaker translation, unmodified: nothing stream-specific was added to the translator for this fixture, since the upstream/resilience mapping does not distinguish which protocol dereferences the pool.

The real-Jul E2E lives in `cmd/jul/corpus_stream_runtime_test.go` (`TestNGINXCorpusStreamUpstreamFailoverRealE2E`) rather than the generic manifest `scenarios` array, because it needs one upstream member that is deliberately never listening (a reserved-then-released loopback port, so every dial against it gets a genuine connection refused) and raw-TCP response inspection, neither of which the generic single-request/response Scenario/Dimension model expresses. It proves: a stream client connection that would otherwise dial the dead backend is transparently retried against the healthy one (Jul's default retry-every-distinct-backend-on-dial-failure behavior, `internal/stream.dialBackend`), the `max_fails=1` breaker then excludes the dead backend for `fail_timeout`, and every one of a run of client connections completes successfully against the healthy backend once the breaker has tripped - the same masking behavior `upstream-failover-runtime` already proves for HTTP, now proven for a raw L4 stream connection where there is no HTTP status code to inspect, only a successful byte-for-byte echo.

This E2E is TCP-only and loopback-only; UDP has no connection-oriented dial-failure/circuit-breaker concept to prove (a UDP stream session has no handshake to fail). No pinned real-NGINX reference lane runs this fixture today (`scripts/nginx-migration-e2e.sh` only exercises HTTP scenarios).
